correctness.rationale: PASS. The exterior derivative DR_p(ru)=r^-1(I-u φ^T), φ_i=sign(u_i)|u_i|^(p-1), and integration on each straight segment proves its supremum is the global Lipschitz constant. Weighted absolute row sums yield 1-a^p+(a/w_i)(Σ_{j≠i}w_j^p)^(1/p)(1-a^p)^((p-1)/p), optimized as F_p(k_i). Weighted column sums yield the conjugate F_{pconj}(k_i). Hölder equality supplies boundary realizing directions; k_i peaks at min weight; the scalar F_s optimizer is unique by strict monotonicity of the derivative equation. Equal weights uniquely minimize B_s, leading dimension orders n^(1/p) and n^(1/pconj), with reversed ordering between n=2 and large n for p≠2.
residual_risks: Exterior derivatives are limiting sharpness: two distinct finite points need not attain the ratio.
No claims for complex spaces, endpoint exponents or nearest-point retractions under the weighted measurement norms.
